A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Label Horizon Paradox study. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover all 30 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-F, with no material gaps.

before.justification: v4 reports original forecasting experiments, horizon analyses, portfolio backtests, and runtime measurements in Sections 3, 5-6 and Appendices E-F.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental and simulation outcomes, including forecasting comparisons, ablations, backtests, and timing results in Tables 1-9 and Figures 2-4.

M1.justification: The warm-up, entropy-regularized bi-level updates, horizon selection, and subsequent retraining in Section 4 are unchanged. The new demo pointer does not document a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CSI 300/500/1000 and S&P 500 coverage, interday and intraday tasks, and market-crash scenario. The added Alpha158 demo link is not accompanied by a reported training or evaluation experiment.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical throughout: the same ten forecasting backbones, Naive Averaging, Equal-Weight MTL, and selected-top-5 variants appear in the corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: The chronological splits, preprocessing, batch construction, optimization settings, metrics, and backtesting procedures in Sections 5.1-5.2 and Appendices A-B and E-F are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions retain identical horizon sweeps, decomposition validation, learned-weight analysis, warm-up ablation, aggregation comparisons, market-crash stress tests, and efficiency analysis.

E5.justification: Five-seed reporting in the benchmark tables and seed-level displays in Figures 2-3 remain unchanged. No uncertainty estimates, run counts, or statistical procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1-9 and plotted results in Figures 2-4 are unchanged, including supplementary intraday, US-market, stress-test, backtesting, and timing results. No demo results are supplied.

T1.justification: The assumptions, theorem, corollary, and mathematical derivations in Section 3 and Appendices C-D are identical. Equations elsewhere in the paper are also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the Label Horizon Paradox, its signal-noise explanation, adaptive supervision, and empirical benefits.

C2.justification: Mechanism interpretations and qualifications remain identical, including the mixed intraday findings in Appendix E.1, fixed signal-direction limitation in Appendix C, and larger-model overhead caveat in Appendix F.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly provides a GitHub link to a demo based on open-source Alpha158 factors. This adds concrete access information absent from v4; the PDFs do not establish the demo's functionality or reproduction coverage.

R1.justification: The literature citations, bibliography, and research positioning in Section 7 are unchanged. The demo announcement adds no cited research work or substantive novelty comparison.

P1.justification: Section 5 gains one sentence announcing the Alpha158-based demo, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. The remaining prose, headings, and main-text/appendix organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added sentence and wrapped hyperlink produce local vertical-spacing adjustments in page 6's right column. All figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The new demo link in Section 5 modestly improves resource discoverability and reproducibility guidance. Scientific content and supporting evidence are unchanged, and the PDFs alone cannot establish whether the demo reproduces the reported experiments.
